question: Recently, displaced refugees and migrants arriving in eastern Crete have been living in inhumane conditions, particularly in Ierapetra and at the AGREEX site. Hundreds of people are being crammed into a totally unsuitable site, in appalling conditions, in tents under refuse collection trucks, exposed to rain, cold and disease, without basic healthcare and medical assistance.

The government, the EU and the local administration bear a heavy responsibility. Negotiations with Libyan chieftains and the EU’s imperialist operation IRINI are exacerbating the problem. The new repressive measures being prepared by the EU and national governments represent another link in the chain of barbarity.
The local community and the people of Crete have responded with solidarity with those who have been displaced. In view of the above: 1.

What is the Commission’s view on the immediate transfer of asylum seekers from the completely unsuitable and overcrowded site in Ierapetra in Crete, and on the temporary establishment of suitably equipped, temporary, open reception facilities in Athanatoi in the prefecture of Heraklion, funded and managed exclusively by the state?

What is the Commission’s view on the full implementation of the Geneva Convention on the Right to Asylum, contrary to the guidelines of the EU Pact on Migration and Asylum, with applications being rejected through fast-track procedures without individual examination?

What is the Commission’s view on the refugees’ travelling to their countries of final destination, so that they are not confined in closed, prison-like facilities and Greece is not turned into a migrant warehouse?
